acts.desc: Ira talks to author Etgar Keret about his mom, and the stories she used to tell him when she put him to sleep. He explains why it's always been so hard to write about her.
acts.credits: By Ira Glass and Etgar Keret
acts.label: Prologue
Story #1
acts.desc: The story Etgar's mother told him, to explain what her father was like.
acts.title: Bedtime Story

acts.label: Story #2
acts.desc: Etgar asks his mother why she only ever strokes his face with the back of her hand.
acts.title: Razor

acts.desc: Etgar tells Ira about his mother’s experience in the Holocaust and why she didn’t like people seeing her as a "survivor" or being defined by those terrible years.
acts.label: Act 3
acts.title: Conversation

acts.label: Story #3
acts.desc: Etgar's mom invents a business for herself where other women look to her like a queen.
acts.title: Fabric

acts.label: Story #4
acts.desc: It rains one morning before Etgar's son goes to school, and he and his wife don't agree on how to handle the situation.
acts.title: Rain Day

acts.label: Story #5
acts.desc: Etgar’s mother and a school bully.
acts.title: Never Forget a Smell

acts.desc: Ira asks Etgar if he has any memories where his mom is not the hero of the story.
acts.label: Act 7
acts.title: Conversation

acts.label: Story #6
acts.desc: Etgar becomes a vegetarian and his mother jumps into action.
acts.title: The Stuff

acts.desc: Etgar mom asks for a disturbing favor.
acts.label: Act 10
acts.title: Conversation

acts.label: Story #7
acts.desc: A story Etgar's mom only told him one time, while very drunk.
acts.title: The First Angel You See

acts.label: Story #8
acts.desc:
Etgar remembers throwing a fit at a restaurant as a little boy, and what his mother said to him.
Most of these stories about Etgar's mom were written for an exhibition about her called " Inside Out " at the Jewish Museum in Berlin. It runs until March 19, 2023. Etgar is the author of Seven Good Years and other books of short stories, and emails a free story to subscribers every week in his newsletter.
acts.title: Good Day
